rejectedKeys: child of Ajax son of Telamon
rationale: F3/DEV-114 reversed-direction shape in variant_claims, verified against the cited source by A11's own criterion (reversed reading attested, correct reading never attested in that source). The Iliad says 'son of Telamon' 22 times and never 'Telamon, son of' anyone; 'Teucer, son of Telamon' at 13.170 and 15.436. So Telamon is the father of both Ajax and Teucer, and every 'Telamon | parentage | child of Ajax/Teucer' row is backwards. Found by DEV-121's verification addendum (8 rows); the two 'child of Teucer' rows are the same shape and were not counted there.

rejectedKeys: son of Telamon, sprung from Zeus
rationale: GAP-007's variant_claims half. Same Homeric vocative formula the deny-list entry suppresses on the relationships side: "Aias, sprung from Zeus, thou son of Telamon, captain of the host", verified live in the corpus at Iliad 7.233, 9.643 and 11.456 -- one real father and one divine honorific in a single line. Extends DEV-112/F2's identical verdict on 'Patroclus | parentage | sprung from Zeus' @ 1.325-1.363 to the other hero the formula names. Telamon is attested as Ajax's father 22 times in the Iliad alone and is already promoted at trust_tier=1 from two sources.

A genuine within-source variant tradition, verified verbatim against Apollodorus 3.12.6: "And Aeacus married Endeis, daughter of Sciron, by whom he had two sons, Peleus and Telamon. But Pherecydes says that Telamon was a friend, not a brother of Peleus, he being a son of Actaeus and Glauce, daughter of Cychreus." One passage, one mythographer, two incompatible parentages, both attributed -- the same shape DEV-119 promoted for Agamemnon/Plisthenes. Found by DEV-122 while triaging Telamon's reversed-direction rows and recorded there as owed work. The corroborating 'child of Aeacus' rows at 1.8.2 / 1.9.16 / ovid 7.469-7.500 / 13.1-13.42 stay at trust_tier=3: they were not read against their own passages in this pass, and promoting on inference is what the review gate exists to prevent.

rationale: A14's repaired self-reference reporting plus A15's first sweep. Each group was read against its own cited passage, not batch-rejected: 11 parentage self-references (nobody can be their own parent), 12 death self-references whose passages name a different agent or no death at all (Elatus is killed by the swineherd at Odyssey 22.268; Eurydice dies 'bitten by a snake'), and 5 reversed death claims mirroring the relationships-layer swaps DEV-123 made via A12. FOUR findings were verified CORRECT and are waived rather than rejected: both Ajax rows encode his SUICIDE ('he came to his senses and slew himself', Apollodorus E.5.7), Amphimedon/Telemachus is a wrist wound not a kill, and Tlepolemus/Sarpedon is the pronoun-anaphora false positive A12 already carries a standing waiver for.

Three self-referential rows the first batch missed, each rejected by exact claim key rather than by subject+source+passage_ref group. Two (`Chryses`, `Telemachus`) sit at a different ref from the rows already rejected; the third (`Amphimedon | killed by Amphimedon`) shares its ref with the CORRECT `Killed by Telemachus` row, so the group-level key had protected it along with its waived sibling -- the same over-broad keying that the tier-1 guard caught earlier in this pass, here caught by A15 still reporting after the batch.

The remaining self-referential parentage rows, surfaced once A14's dedup key was corrected to include passage_ref. Nobody can be their own parent, so unlike A15's death equivalent (where suicide makes self-reference legitimate) these need no passage read. The Chryses rows are a plain extraction slip: the daughter is Chryseis, and 'Chryses | daughter of Chryses' collapses the two names.

Zeus is not the child of Athena -- she is his daughter, born from his head, in every source in this corpus. A14 could not see these four rows until it was taught the curated alias map (DEV-126): the claim value spells her 'Athene' (Murray's Iliad and Evelyn-White's Hymns), which is an entity_aliases/known_aliases entry, not a confirmed entity name, so parse_parent resolved nobody and the rows counted as unparsed. The six sibling rows spelling her 'Athena' were already reviewed and rejected to trust_tier=2 by an earlier hand pass -- the same false claim was caught on one spelling and invisible on the other, which is the asymmetry this fix removes. Verified per row against its own cited passage rather than by reasoning from the claim: Hymns 5.7 states the correct direction outright ('the daughter of Zeus who holds the aegis, bright-eyed Athene'), Iliad 5.733 likewise ('Athene, daughter of Zeus that beareth the aegis'), and Iliad 21.416 names Zeus's actual father ('Zeus, son of Cronos'). The fourth, Iliad 5.864-5.907, is a different defect in the same row set -- its passage states no parentage at all ('Alalcomenean Athene'), so it is unsupported by its own citation (the DEV-098 shape) rather than reversed. All four are tier 3, so nothing seeded changes.
